key_insights.body: 3D pillar-layer framework with Co(II)-aminotriazole layers and mbdc2- pillars; noninterpenetrated pcu network → stability

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: hydrogen-bonded network involving coordinated water, free water, carboxylate oxygen atoms, and amino groups of ATAZ → stability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] select organic ligands and metal ions with suitable coordination geometries → crucial to preparation of target compounds

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use a mixed-ligand self-assembly strategy combining isophthalic acid and 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole → effective for constructing coordination polymers; the chosen ligands were selected to enable target framework construction

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: methylene blue degradation system with compound 1 catalyst present vs methylene blue degradation system without compound 1 catalyst: winner=subject_a on methylene_blue_degradation

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] increase temperature beyond 350 °C: the framework collapses

notable_quotes: MB shows no obvious degradation without compound 1, supporting that the observed photodegradation depends on the catalyst.
Compound 1 is an active photocatalyst for methylene blue degradation: MB conversion reaches 89% after 120 min under UV irradiation.
The framework is only thermally stable up to a point; beyond 350 °C it begins to collapse because the organic ligands decompose.
